name: Nile
tagline: Serverless Postgres that makes tenants a first-class primitive, with per-tenant isolation and placement.
description: Nile is a managed PostgreSQL service designed for B2B SaaS, where the tenant is a built-in concept rather than a column you remember to filter on. Tables marked as tenant-aware are partitioned by tenant behind the scenes, connections can be scoped to a tenant for automatic isolation, and each tenant can be placed on shared or dedicated compute and moved without application changes. It also bundles tenant-aware auth and pgvector for per-tenant AI features. The free plan has no pause and 1 GB of storage, and Pro starts at $15 per month. It is a niche but thoughtful option when multi-tenancy is the hardest part of your data model; several roadmap items such as branching are still labeled as coming soon.

pricing.notes: Free: 1 GB storage, 50M query tokens, no pausing. Pro: 5 GB, 150M query tokens, 99.95% SLA. Scale from $350/month; Enterprise custom.

scale.notes: Tenants are distributed across Postgres instances and can be moved between shared and dedicated compute.

strengths: Tenant isolation enforced by the database, not application filters
Move a tenant to dedicated compute without code changes
weaknesses: Small vendor; long-term viability is a real consideration
Some Postgres features and extensions are restricted
Branching and provisioned compute still on the roadmap
Only valuable if your app is genuinely multi-tenant
useCases: B2B SaaS with many customer organizations
Moving large customers to isolated infrastructure
